name: Adversarial Carbon Brief
description: Same structure as carbon_budget_brief but with four embedded attacks to test the trust model: (1) fabricated citation, (2) contradicted claim, (3) cherry-picked scope, (4) near-duplicate self-verify. Each claim is pre-labeled in EXPECTED_VERDICTS below. Used by tests/test_adversarial_packet.py and by manual live-runs.

attack_1_fabricated.description: Citation [3] points to a source document that was never uploaded.
attack_1_fabricated.reason: anchor resolver should mark as unresolvable_anchor; pipeline short-circuits to needs_review.

attack_2_contradicted.description: Claim says global CO2 emissions DECREASED 12% in 2022; source_01 says they INCREASED.
attack_2_contradicted.reason: the source explicitly says the opposite. Classifier must catch this as contradicted, not insufficient_support.

attack_3_cherry_picked.description: Claim asserts a fact that's true for ONE sub-component but phrased as if about the whole system.
attack_3_cherry_picked.reason: evidence only partially supports — trust-model rule VERDICT-02 says partial evidence must route to insufficient_support, never supported.

attack_4_self_verify.description: Claim has no citation marker. Retrieval will self-verify against the report itself, and the only 'supporting' span is the claim's own paragraph in different words.
attack_4_self_verify.reason: three-layer defense: (1) position-overlap filter excludes the paragraph containing the claim, (2) classifier prompt sees SAME DOCUMENT AS CLAIM tag, (3) 0.80 cap + 0.70 threshold routes weak matches to needs_review.
